The assistant recommended a refundable Sheraton hold because all conference events are now in the building, with Hampton retained as backup if the refrigerator or mini-fridge cannot be confirmed.

messages.content: The Denver block closes tomorrow. Hampton dropped a little, but Sheraton is still about $40 more per night. Since the Wednesday roundtable moved into the same building, can you compare the real totals?

Using two nights and normal local transfers:
| Hotel | Est. room tax + transfers | Food and room notes | Trade-off |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Hampton Inn & Suites Denver Downtown-Convention Center | $465-$485 | Breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed; easy casual dinner nearby | Short walk or quick ride to reception/sessions; not in the roundtable building |
| Sheraton Denver Downtown event block | $545-$570 | Breakfast paid; on-site/16th Street dinner options; refrigerator appears to require confirmation | About $70-$95 net premium, but all Monday-Wednesday conference pieces are in the building |
Recommendation: hold Sheraton if the rate is refundable and you can get the refrigerator or mini-fridge confirmed before releasing Hampton.
Breakfast is the part finance will notice. Does that make Hampton the cleaner answer?

Not automatically. Hampton is cheaper, especially after breakfast, but the Sheraton premium buys no daily conference transfer, no weather issue, and no Wednesday checkout shuffle before the roundtable. I would frame it as a conference-site lodging choice, not a luxury upgrade.
What exactly should I check before clicking the Sheraton hold?

Check: refundable cancellation deadline, whether a refrigerator or mini-fridge can be confirmed for your room type, whether a coffee maker is in the room, any destination or amenity fee, and breakfast cost/hours. Also confirm the block rate includes standard Wi-Fi.
If they say the fridge is request-only, not guaranteed?

Then place the Sheraton hold only if it is cancellable, call the block desk first thing, and keep Hampton as the backup until you get a clear answer. If the fridge remains purely request-only, switch to Hampton before its lower rate moves.

messages.content: I held the Sheraton block with the fridge request. The organizer now says Wednesday ends at 11:15. Can you refresh the Denver flights before I ticket?

Yes. I would ignore DEN departures before about 2:15. Short list:
| Itinerary | Fare | Timing |
|---|---:|---|
| United nonstop ORD-DEN Mon 9:55a-11:35a; DEN-ORD Wed 2:35p-5:50p | about $318 | Clean for reception and post-roundtable checkout/transfer |
| Later one-stop return, dep. about 5:20p, ORD about 10:55p | about $238 | Saves about $80 but makes Wednesday long |
Best pick: the nonstop.
So pay the $80?
Yes. The 2:35-ish nonstop is worth it here: 11:15 end, checkout, and the DEN transfer leave little room for earlier flights, while the connection saves money but gets you home unnecessarily late.

messages.content: Next trip: Omaha, July 16-18, flying from Chicago. I have a Wednesday afternoon intro, Thursday split between a museum education program and a library partner, and a Friday debrief that should end by 11:30. I would rather avoid a rental car if rideshares look reasonable. Hotel under about $185 before tax, ideally downtown or near the Thursday morning venue. Please include breakfast, in-room coffee/mini-fridge, and dinner access in the comparison.

I can build that. A few location details will make the commute estimates useful: what neighborhoods are the Wednesday intro, Thursday museum, Thursday library, and Friday debrief in? Also, is the Wednesday meeting fixed-time or is there some arrival flexibility?

Wednesday is 2:30 in Benson. Thursday museum starts at 9 near downtown/midtown, then the library partner is in South Omaha after lunch. Friday debrief is downtown from 10 to 11:30. I will be carry-on only.

Good. That points to a downtown or Old Market base, not an airport hotel. Rideshares should be workable for this pattern: airport-downtown about 10-15 minutes, downtown-Benson about 15-20, and downtown-South Omaha about 12-18. Flight framing:
| Arrival choice | Timing | Cost/impact |
|---|---|---|
| Wed. July 16 morning | ORD-OMA nonstop around 8:20a-9:55a; return Fri. around 1:50p | Lowest trip cost; enough cushion for 2:30 if the flight runs normally |
| Tue. July 15 evening | ORD-OMA nonstop around 5:55p-7:25p; same Friday return | More relaxed start, but adds one hotel night and dinner; roughly $210-$240 more all-in |
Please put the hotels into the same finance view. They will ask for all-in, not just room rate.

Assuming Wednesday arrival, two hotel nights, airfare around $260-$285, and $95-$120 in rideshares:
| Hotel | 2-night room total with tax | Food/room basics | Commute and dinner notes | Est. trip total |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Hampton Inn & Suites Omaha-Downtown | $370-$390 | Breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed | North downtown; short ride to Old Market dinner; good for museum/debrief | $725-$795 |
| Holiday Inn Express & Suites Omaha Downtown - Old Market area | $350-$375 | Breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed, verify room type | Cheapest; decent downtown/midtown access; dinner is a walk or short ride | $705-$780 |
| Embassy Suites Old Market | $430-$455 | Breakfast included; suite wet bar/fridge and coffee; on-site restaurant | Best dinner access and easiest Friday downtown logistics | $785-$860 |
| Cambria Omaha Downtown | $395-$420 | Breakfast paid; fridge and coffee listed; on-site restaurant | Good dinner convenience, but less attractive if breakfast matters | $750-$825 |
The Embassy rate is right at the cap. Is it worth that over Hampton?

Only if the refundable rate stays at or below the cap before tax and there is no surprise fee. Embassy buys the easiest dinner plan and a stronger breakfast setup, but Hampton gives most of the practical value for less. I would not chase Embassy if it jumps even $10-$15.
I do not need fancy. I just do not want to be stuck hunting for dinner after a site day.

Then Hampton or Holiday Inn Express should be fine. Plan on Old Market, Capitol District, or Blackstone by short rideshare if you do not feel like walking. Cambria is the restaurant-on-site choice, but paying for breakfast weakens it.
Which ones clearly show both coffee maker and mini-fridge?

Hampton and Embassy are the clearest from the room descriptions: in-room coffee plus refrigerator or suite wet bar/fridge. Holiday Inn Express also appears to list both for standard rooms, but I would verify the exact room type before booking. Ask the desk: refrigerator in the room, not just available on request; coffee maker in the room; weekday breakfast start time; and cancellation deadline.
On flights, arriving Wednesday morning saves a lot, but ORD in July makes me nervous.

That is the real trade-off. The early nonstop gives roughly four hours between scheduled landing and the Benson meeting, so a normal delay is survivable. A cancellation or two-hour-plus delay would be painful. Since you said you can travel carry-on and the intro is at 2:30, Wednesday morning is reasonable unless that meeting becomes non-negotiable at the exact start time.
What if I could join as late as 3:15 but not after that?

That keeps Wednesday morning viable. Book the earliest nonstop, not a late-morning flight, and avoid a connection. If the early nonstop is canceled the night before, you can still pivot to a Tuesday evening or very early Wednesday alternative; if you wait for a later Wednesday departure, you lose that cushion.
Should I check Midway, or is ORD cleaner for Omaha?

Check Midway only as a fare sanity check. For this schedule, ORD is cleaner because the useful nonstop times line up better. A cheaper one-stop from Midway would not be worth the connection risk on the outbound or the later return.
And Friday, is the 1:50 return too early after an 11:30 debrief?

It works. Downtown to OMA is usually short, and with carry-on you could leave around 11:45 and still have a reasonable airport cushion. I would skip anything around 12:30, but 1:50 is a good after-lunch return; 4:40 is safe but wastes the afternoon.
Can you give me the final shortlist and recommendation in one compact table?

| Piece | Recommendation | Estimate | Trade-off |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Flights | Wed. July 16 ORD-OMA earliest nonstop around 8:20a; return Fri. July 18 around 1:50p | $260-$285 | Saves the Tuesday hotel night; enough cushion for Benson if the flight is reasonably on time |
| Hotel | Hampton Inn & Suites Omaha-Downtown, refundable, 2 nights | $370-$390 with tax | Breakfast included; coffee and mini-fridge listed; dinner requires a short walk or ride |
| Local transport | Rideshares, no rental car | $95-$120 | Works for downtown, Benson, and South Omaha; schedule the Thursday morning ride rather than waiting last-minute |
| Estimated total | Flight + hotel + rideshares | $725-$795 | Practical and below the lodging target |
| Backup | Embassy Suites Old Market if it stays under $185 before tax | $785-$860 total | Better dinner access and breakfast, but only worth it if the rate does not creep up |

Recommendation: book the Wednesday-morning nonstop plus Hampton refundable. Use Tuesday evening arrival only if the Wednesday intro becomes firm enough that a delay would damage the visit.
